scenario: AITA for being home all day and refusing to cook for my mom? | I'm a female in my senior year of high school and I have a younger sister in grade 10. As most of you know, schools have been closed for a while now and won't reopen for at least another month. My dad gets to work from home, but my mom still has to go out to her office. My school just started online teaching, and we've been getting a lot of assignments to complete. However, my mom expects us to make dinner basically every night because "we're home all day". That really annoyed me because yeah "we're home all day" but we have school work to do. I got upset and asked her why doesn't she cook, since she always finishes work at 5 pm and her office is like 6 minutes from home. Well, once she got home today and saw there was no dinner prepared, she got pissed and started screaming at me how she's so ashamed of us and how we're useless. When I explained how yes we're home all day but doesn't mean we have the whole day off, she got even more mad and said that it doesn't take that long to cook. I refuted by "why don't you cook then?" For more context, my mom is an awful cook. She literally puts no effort into learning or looking up recipes. My dad is an excellent cook. He's tried to teach her before, but she refuses to learn and complains. Before, he would cook for us almost every day, even if he came home late from work (he has a high demanding job so his hours range but he's home 6 pm the EARLIEST, sometimes as late as 9 or even 10 pm. + 30-40 minutes one way commuting). And what does he come home to? Either a low effort flavourless meal from my mom, or my mom sitting on her ass watching TV and asking him what's he's gonna make for dinner. So my dad is forced to make dinner at a late hour so he can eat. More recently, he would just eat fast-food before coming home because he doesn't expect dinner to be on the table. However, he asks if us girls are hungry and offers to cook something for us to eat because he's worried that our mom didn't make us a proper meal. I'm a good cook too (self taught), and I try to help out if I don't have too much homework to do. I did a lot of the cooking during the first 3 weeks before online school started, as well as baking lots of treats like breads, cookies, meringues etc. Also, my dad does practically all the chores in the house, while my mom spends all her time sitting on her ass watching TV. So AITA for not cooking dinner today and telling my mom to not expect dinner every time she comes home? Also, my dad ended cooking in the end today.

My mom works from home, but she still goes out to her office every day, which is only 6 minutes away. She gets home at 5 PM, and I guess she expects us to have dinner ready by then. But we're both in high school, dealing with online classes and assignments, so it's not like we have the whole day off. I got really annoyed one night because there was no dinner prepared, and my mom started yelling at us, saying we're useless and she's ashamed of us. I tried to explain that just because we're home all day doesn't mean we have the whole day off, but she didn't listen. She even said that cooking doesn't take that long, and I retorted by asking why she doesn't cook then. From what I know, my mom is an awful cook. She doesn't put any effort into learning or looking up recipes, and my dad has tried to teach her before, but she refuses. My dad is an excellent cook and used to make dinner almost every day, even when he came home late from work. But now, he's forced to make dinner at a late hour because my mom doesn't contribute. Lately, he's been eating fast food before coming home because he doesn't expect dinner to be on the table. I'm also a good cook, self-taught, and I try to help out if I don't have too much homework. I did a lot of the cooking during the first few weeks before online school started, and I even baked a lot of treats like breads, cookies, and meringues. My dad does practically all the chores in the house, while my mom spends all her time sitting around watching TV. So, I'm feeling really frustrated and wondering if it's AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) for not cooking dinner today and telling my mom not to expect dinner every time she comes home. My dad ended up cooking in the end today. I need to figure out if my actions are justified or if I'm being unreasonable. On one hand, I have schoolwork to do, and it's not fair that my mom expects me to cook every night. On the other hand, I'm part of the family, and contributing to household chores is expected. But my mom doesn't seem to be contributing at all, and my dad is already doing so much. I'm also trying to balance my responsibilities with my schoolwork, which is already overwhelming. Maybe I should communicate my feelings more clearly to my mom instead of just refusing to cook. I need to explain that I have schoolwork and that I can't always be available to cook. Perhaps we can find a compromise where we take turns cooking or find other ways to contribute to the household. It's also frustrating that my mom doesn't seem to acknowledge the effort my dad and I put into cooking and doing chores. I wonder if other people in similar situations feel the same way. It's tough when one parent isn't pulling their weight, and it puts extra pressure on the other parent and the children. I need to find a way to assert my boundaries without feeling guilty for not being able to cook every night. Maybe setting clear expectations and responsibilities within the family can help alleviate some of the tension. Overall, I think my frustration is valid, but I need to approach the situation more calmly and communicate my needs effectively. It's important to address the imbalance in responsibilities and find a solution that works for everyone. I don't want to be seen as uncooperative, but I also don't want to be the only one taking on all the responsibilities.
